args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production release (error rate was 0.18). I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback status: healthy, version v2.3.0 in all regions, error rate 0.002. Not yet done: root-cause analysis of v2.3.1. v2.3.1-rc was healthy in staging only and was not used. Follow-up needed before re-deploying v2.3.1: investigate the regression and get change-manager approval if v2.3.1 is re-released, since it has no healthy production history.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Why v2.3.0:** It is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1 is the unhealthy release. v2.3.1-rc was healthy only in staging, so I did not use it. The rollback didn't need change-manager approval because v2.3.0 has a healthy production history.
- **Result:** The service now reports healthy on v2.3.0 in every region, with the error rate down from 0.18 to 0.002.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the rollback and the post-rollback state. It also notes that v2.3.1 still needs root-cause analysis, and that re-releasing it will require change-manager approval because it has never been healthy in production.

content.text: The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1 is the unhealthy release, and v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging. Since v2.3.0 has been healthy in production, the rollback doesn't need change-manager approval. Rolling back now.
